newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ATLETICO SAY JUNINHO POISED TO SIGN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATLETICO SAY JUNINHO POISED TO SIGN.

text.p: Atletico Madrid owner Jesus Gil said on Tuesday that he believed it would be very hard for Juninho to sign for any other team.
Other reports from Spain claimed the deal was already completed.

In England, Tottenham have made a late bid to prise the Brazilian midfielder away from Middlesbrough -- and Atletico -- and have had an offer of 11 million pounds ($18.3 million) accepted by Middlesbrough.

Juninho has not agreed personal terms with Tottenham, and according to reports in Spain, Atletico have already reached agreement with him. They have apparantly offered 12 million pounds ($20 million) and they expect to hear on Wednesday that the deal is done.

"I believe that it is difficult for him to sign for any other team in the world," Gil was quoted as saying, while a report in the sports daily Marca said agreement had already been reached between Atletico and the Brazilian.
The Spanish press also carried comments from Juninho's father and manager Osvaldo Giroldo saying that he would join Atletico.
Middlesbrough, who say the only deal they have agreed is one with Tottenham, hold the key to any transfer.
But the situation is fluid with Atletico -- apparantly backed by Osvaldo Giroldo -- looking the more likely to win the battle for his signature -- at least according to the Spanish press.
Marca quoted Osvaldo Giroldo as saying: "Juninho will play for Atletico. He is having a holiday in Brazil and next week we will go to Madrid to pass the necessary medical.
"Atletico and Middlesbrough reached agreement on Sunday with my approval. It is true that at the end a great offer came from Tottenham, but my son wants to play in Spain and with Atletico Madrid.
"Miguel Angel Gil (director general, son of Jesus Gil) has shown us special affection and attention. Juninho already feels himself an Atletico player."
The article also states that Middlesbrough chairman Steve Gibson agreed to the transfer over the phone with Miguel Angel Gil, for a million pounds more than Tottenham's bid.
"We sent a fax yesterday and they will answer us tomorrow -- Wednesday," said Gil.

But earlier on Tuesday Tottenham appeared to have gained the upper hand in their battle to sign the midfielder when Middlesbrough said they were involved in negotiations only with their fellow English club.
"We've accepted a written bid from Tottenham for 11 million pounds ($18.3 milion)," said Dave Allen, Middlesbrough's public relations officer.
"It depends on whether he can agree personal terms with Spurs. It's up to him and Spurs to get together.
"He's a Middlesbrough player at the moment," said Allen. "He certainly hasn't signed for Tottenham."

Juninho, who is under contract to Middlesbrough for another two years, is keen to leave after the club were relegated from the premier league last season. He has repeatedly said he favours a move to Spain where he feels greater exposure on television in Brazil will increase his chances of making the national squad for the 1998 World Cup finals.

Allen dismissed a report in Britain's Sun newspaper that Juninho would move to Tottenham for one season, while Middlesbrough attempted to win back their premier league place, and then return to see out his contract.
"There is no truth in that," he said.
